finding_key: docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md::two independently-tracked issues are landed in one change, against the task plan's own instruction to keep them apart
evidence: The diff really does carry both work streams at once: docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:17-22 says the loopback/PKCE work is being redone "as its own change" after a first attempt "shipped inside the #661 error-envelope branch and was reverted", yet the same diff adds docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md plus the full `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope`/`commandPath` refactor across ~25 CLI files (formatter.ts, cli.ts, api-keys/cells/docs/notes/slides/tabs/files, docs//notes//slides/import.ts, files/upload.ts, files/download.ts, schema.ts, ctx.ts) alongside the backend guard/store/controller and login.ts nonce+PKCE changes. The two are functionally independent — the only overlap is that login.ts's new `failFromBackend` uses `backendErrorEnvelope`, an #661-scope conversion, not something PKCE requires. One nuance the claim overstates: the doc attributes the earlier revert to the work being *half-done* (no PKCE, no guard tests, hard nonce requirement), not to bundling per se, so "the plan's own instruction to keep them apart" is an inference rather than a literal instruction; still, "done as its own change" is contradicted by the diff. Impact is on reviewability/revertability of a security-sensitive change rather than on behavior, so I rate it minor.
